title: Perverse amplitude of the Fourier transform
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let $V=V^\vee=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, let
$p_1,p_2:V\times_{k_0}V^\vee\to V,V^\vee$ be the projections of the
Fourier square, and let $\mathcal K_\psi$ be the
Fourier kernel of [def-fd-kernel]. The
Fourier–Deligne transform

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi=p_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*(-)\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)[1]
$$

of [def-fd-transform] has perverse amplitude at most one on both
sides with respect to the perverse candidate subcategories of
[def-per-perverse-subcategories]:

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(V)\bigr)\subset
{}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee),\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl({}^pD^{\ge0}(V)\bigr)\subset
{}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee),
$$

hence maps the perverse heart candidate of [def-per-perverse-subcategories]
into the strip ${}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee)\cap{}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee)$.

proof.text: Put $X=V\times_{k_0}V^\vee=\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x,\xi]$. Under [def-sbc-affine-space], $p_1$ and $p_2$ are respectively the relative affine lines $\mathbf A^1_V\to V$ and $\mathbf A^1_{V^\vee}\to V^\vee$. By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] both are smooth of constant relative dimension one. This also applies over each geometric point, since that lemma allows every base scheme: their geometric fibers are smooth of pure dimension one, in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The affine charts are polynomial rings in one variable over the target chart, so both projections are affine and of finite type; their relative diagonals are cut out by the difference of the two fiber coordinates, hence closed. The same description over $k_0$ shows that $V,V^\vee,X$ are separated of finite type. These verify the geometric hypotheses of the two permanence lemmas below, using the morphism conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: paragraphs 1 and 3: geometry of the two projections

proof.text: Take $K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(V)$, or separately $K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(V)$, in the bounded constructible coefficient category implicit in [def-per-perverse-subcategories]. Apply [lem-per-smooth-pullback-t-exact] to $p_1$ with $d=1$. It says exactly that $Lp_1^*K[1]$ lies in the corresponding class of index zero on $X$. Therefore $Lp_1^*K$ lies in ${}^pD^{\le1}(X)$, respectively ${}^pD^{\ge1}(X)$, because [def-per-perverse-subcategories] defines the index-$1$ class to be the index-zero class shifted by $[-1]$. In particular $[-1]$ raises the index from $0$ to $1$.

source.place: paragraph 1: smooth pullback and shift convention

proof.text: By [prop-kernel-lisse], the kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ is lisse of rank one and has finite Tor amplitude. The scheme $X=\mathbf A^2_{k_0}$ is smooth of pure dimension two, by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] with $n=2$, so the hypothesis on $X$ in [lem-per-lisse-tensor-permanence] holds. Apply its explicitly stated shifted versions to the corresponding conclusion of step 2. For $H:=Lp_1^*K\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi$ this gives $H\in{}^pD^{\le1}(X)$, respectively $H\in{}^pD^{\ge1}(X)$. Both sides of this invocation use the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ statement of the permanence node; no identification with a finite-coefficient Lean category is made.

source.place: paragraph 2: lisse kernel and tensor permanence

proof.text:
For the affine bound we need the natural comparison
\(Rp_{2,!}(H[1])\cong(Rp_{2,!}H)[1]\). The adic coefficient convention
[def-fourier-set], under which the \(\otimes^L_E\) and the
compact-support direct image \(Rf_!=Rf_*\circ j_!\) (read through a
compactification) of the transform are taken on the derived-complete
constructible categories \(D^b_c(-,E)\), not on discrete sheaves, binds the
\(p_{2,!}\) of [def-fd-transform] to the compact-support operation on the
rational finite-stage categories. Since \(V\times_{k_0}V^\vee\) and
\(V^\vee\) are noetherian, the open immersion
\(\mathbf A^1\times\mathbf A^1\subset\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf A^1\) of the
standard compactification of \(p_2\) is quasi-compact, and \(\ell\ne p\) is
invertible, so the hypotheses of the next lemma hold. At the
integral stage [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction]
says that the chosen-compactification compact-support operation is an
exact \(\mathcal O_E\)-linear functor on the compatible constructible
category. By the definition of an exact functor in
[def-weil-triangulated-category], this includes a natural shift
isomorphism \(Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}(T[1])\simeq(Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}T)[1]\).
The rational transport [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] carries this
comparison to every finite coefficient field. The coefficient-coherence
statement [lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence] says
that these rational compact-support comparisons commute with shifts and
with every scalar-extension map. Therefore, for a \(\overline{\mathbf
Q}_\ell\)-object represented at a finite stage, the shift isomorphisms are
compatible with all reduction maps and with restriction of scalars, and
remain compatible after passage to a common finite stage. By the
common-stage definition [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], this compatible
family is an isomorphism in the common-stage category \(D^b_c(V^\vee,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\) of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. This proves the required comparison without identifying a
shifted Roos cone with an unshifted one or choosing a non-functorial
isomorphism.

source.place: paragraph 3: compact-support direct image commutes with shifts

proof.text:
By step 3 and [def-per-perverse-subcategories], \(H[1]\) lies in the
corresponding index-zero class. Under the convention of
[def-fourier-set], the morphism along which the transform integrates is exactly \(p_2:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\times
\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\), interpreted in the adic
\(D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\) category by its common finite-stage
construction. It is affine of relative dimension one, so the two displayed
inclusions of [lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve] give
\(Rp_{2,!}(H[1])\in{}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee)\) for the support input and
\(Rp_{2,!}(H[1])\in{}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee)\) for the cosupport input. By
step 4 this is isomorphic to \((Rp_{2,!}H)[1]\), which is precisely
\(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\) by [def-fd-transform] with rank \(r=1\).
Thus the two claimed inclusions hold for their respective inputs.

source.place: paragraph 3: affine amplitude and the normalization [1]

proof.text: If $K$ lies in the perverse heart candidate, [def-per-perverse-subcategories] says that it satisfies both input conditions. The two inclusions just proved therefore put the same object $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)$ in both ${}^pD^{\le1}(V^\vee)$ and ${}^pD^{\ge-1}(V^\vee)$, hence in their intersection. No existence of truncation functors or a perverse t-structure is needed for this intersection argument.

source.place: concluding sentence: heart candidate maps into the strip

tool_uses.why: Generic geometric fact verifies the affine-line projections and the smooth pure-dimensional surface; it does not replace the Fourier argument.
Kernel lissity and finite Tor amplitude are generic input to tensor permanence and are supplied by the kernel unit.
Generic exact compact-support operation on the compatible integral category supplies the shift comparison; this unit has no replacement.
Generic scalar localization transports the integral compact-support shift to finite rational coefficient stages.
Generic compact-support coefficient coherence makes the finite-stage shift comparisons natural and compatible with scalar extensions.
Generic common-stage construction assembles the compatible finite-stage shift maps into the Qlbar-category isomorphism.

The statement matches the blueprint verbatim, is not weakened, and is true (FT is in fact t-exact). I tested it on δ_0→Q̄_ℓ[1], Q̄_ℓ[1]→δ_0(-1) and 0. Steps: (1) the projections are relative A^1 by def-sbc-affine-space; sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth gives relative dimension 1 for them and dimension 2 for X. (2) lem-per-smooth-pullback-t-exact with d=1 and the convention ^pD^{≤n}=^pD^{≤0}[-n]; the signs check. (3) prop-kernel-lisse gives a lisse rank-one kernel, and lem-per-lisse-tensor-permanence (shifted form) applies on the smooth A^2. (4) The shift comparison for Rp_{2,!} comes from the exact integral functor of lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction (j quasi-compact since the schemes are noetherian, ℓ≠p), the exact-functor shift of def-weil-triangulated-category, prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport ('localized shift comparison'), the shift-commuting b^h of lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence, and the common-stage shift of def-weil-pbc-qbar-category; each node says what the step takes from it. (5) lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve with d=1 gives ≤1 and ≥-1. (6) The heart clause is an elementary intersection. But the item used that base-change theorem only for its coefficient-convention sentence, so I replaced it in steps 4 and 5 with the convention definition def-fourier-set (no dependencies).
